_metadata.description: Structured regulatory database for ingredient risk assessment. Risk levels are determined by regulatory status, not opinion.

ingredients.regulation: Requires warning label in EU ('may have adverse effect on activity and attention in children'). Banned in some EU products for children.
Banned in cosmetics and external drugs by FDA. IARC Group 3 carcinogen. Thyroid tumor concerns in animal studies.
Requires warning label in EU. Linked to hyperactivity in children. Banned in Norway and Austria.
Requires warning label in EU. Banned in Norway and Finland. Linked to hyperactivity in children.
Banned in several EU countries. Some studies suggest potential for chromosomal damage.
Restricted in Norway. Brain tumor concerns in animal studies.
IARC Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans). Banned in Japan. Restricted in EU cosmetics.
ingredients.source: IARC Monographs, EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III

ingredients.regulation: Banned in Japan, Australia, and some EU countries for food. Potential endocrine disruptor.
Restricted to 0.02% in EU. Linked to vision disturbances and liver effects at high doses.
Forms nitrosamines (IARC Group 1 carcinogens) when heated with amino acids. Restricted concentrations in EU.
Converts to nitrite in body. Associated with colorectal cancer risk. Restricted in EU baby foods.
Same concerns as sodium nitrite. Restricted concentrations in EU.
Converts to nitrite. Restricted in EU, especially for infant foods.
IARC Group 2B carcinogen. Banned in EU, UK, Canada, Brazil, China. Still allowed in US.
Banned in EU, Japan, India. FDA revoked GRAS status in 2024. Bioaccumulates in tissue.
Banned by FDA (2018). Banned in EU, Canada. WHO goal to eliminate by 2023. Major cardiovascular risk.
Restricted concentration in EU cosmetics. Endocrine disruptor concerns. Banned in Denmark for children's products.
ingredients.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex V, Denmark

ingredients.regulation: Banned in EU cosmetics for children under 3 (leave-on products). Endocrine disruptor.
Banned in EU cosmetics. Strongest estrogenic activity among parabens.
Banned in EU cosmetics due to insufficient safety data.
Banned by FDA in consumer antiseptic washes. Banned in EU cosmetics (most uses). Endocrine disruptor.
Banned by FDA in consumer antiseptic washes. Environmental persistence concerns.
IARC Group 1 carcinogen. Severely restricted in EU cosmetics. Banned in Japan cosmetics.
Releases formaldehyde. Restricted in EU. Banned in Japan and Sweden.
Releases formaldehyde. Restricted in EU. Banned in Japan.
Releases formaldehyde. Restricted concentration in EU.
Releases formaldehyde. Restricted concentration in EU.
Banned in Hawaii, Key West, Palau, US Virgin Islands (coral reef damage). Endocrine disruptor. Restricted in EU.
Banned in Hawaii and Palau. Endocrine disruptor. Coral reef toxicity.
IARC Group 1 carcinogen. Restricted in EU cosmetics. Banned in EU food.
Banned by FDA in cosmetics (2022). Neurotoxin. Banned in EU cosmetics.
ingredients.source: FDA 2022 ruling, EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex II

ingredients.regulation: Banned in EU cosmetics. California Prop 65 listed. Reproductive toxicant.
ingredients.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex II, Prop 65

ingredients.regulation: ECHA SVHC. Banned in EU cosmetics. Reproductive toxicant.
ingredients.source: EU REACH, EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex II

ingredients.regulation: Under review by ECHA. Endocrine disruptor concerns. Often hidden under 'fragrance'.
Banned in EU, Japan, Australia OTC cosmetics. FDA proposed ban. Carcinogen concerns.
ingredients.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex II, FDA

ingredients.regulation: IARC Group 1 carcinogen. Banned globally. Contaminant risk in talc products.
IARC Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic). Endocrine disruptor. Restricted in EU cosmetics.
ingredients.source: IARC Monographs, EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III

ingredients.regulation: Sensitizer and potential mutagen. Restricted in EU cosmetics. Must not contact skin directly.
ingredients.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III, SCCS opinions

ingredients.regulation: Strong allergen and sensitizer. IARC Group 3. Banned in direct skin contact products in EU. Max 2% in hair dyes.
ingredients.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III, IARC Monographs

ingredients.regulation: Endocrine disruptor concerns. Restricted concentration in EU cosmetics.
ingredients.source: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex V, SCCS opinions
